dedupe_keys.name: urban water supply system resilience under earthquake scenarios 27 scenarios and two repair strategies scientific reports 2022

description: This case study is a Scientific Reports paper on the resilience of an existing water distribution network under seismic hazard, motivated by rising threats to water supply and damage to ageing pipes in past earthquakes. An earthquake generation model is coupled with a probabilistic flow-based pressure-driven demand hydraulic model and applied to an existing network, simulating 27 earthquake scenarios and two repair strategies. Resilience is judged from pressure, leak demand, water serviceability and population impacted. Nodal pressure falls below nominal and reaches zero in some scenarios, leak demand could exceed 10 cubic metres per second within hours of an earthquake, and water serviceability drops to a low of about 40 percent. Coverage: one real network, the location of which is given in the full text, not the abstract read here. Access: free article; licence CC-BY-4.0 (article). Caveats: simulated, not observed, damage, and only the abstract was read. It informs seismic resilience and repair-priority simulation for drinking water networks, and relates to the PTSNet transient model in the catalogue.
